name: Craftsman Farms (the Log House)

dates.note: Wikipedia: 'Craftsman Farms is a log house built in 1911'; the craftsman node's exemplar gives 1908-1911 (Stickley began acquiring the land in 1908 per the same article). Both kept.

refs.title: NRHP reference No. 85003730; added April 10, 1989; designated NHL December 14, 1990 (as the Wikipedia infobox prints it)
refs.note: Read from the infobox, not from the National Register's own database.

refs.title: Craftsman Farms - Wikipedia
refs.note: Its own words: 'The focal point of his "Garden of Eden" was a large, log house constructed of hewn chestnut logs found on-site and local stone also found on-site.'

refs.title: [PDF] National Register of Historic Places Registration Form - NPGallery
refs.note: The registration form. Its own words: 'This style consisted of building simple houses of natural materials -- logs, field-stones, and wood shingles -- in harmony with the natural setting.'

note: No HABS survey was found (query: 'Craftsman Farms OR Stickley Morris Plains Parsippany HABS NJ survey log house' on loc.gov returned unrelated New Jersey surveys), so there is no survey block. Also named, without a precedent key, by arts-and-crafts-american. Seeded 4 Sep 2026.
